summary: Describes BGP autonomous system confederations, a technique for splitting a large autonomous system into smaller sub-systems. BGP normally requires every speaker in an AS to be fully meshed, which scales badly. Confederations reduce that burden. It is a draft standard, a standards-track status.

plainLanguage.summary: A large BGP autonomous system can be divided into smaller Member-ASes that exchange routes internally. Outside peers see the confederation as one autonomous system, so they do not need to know its internal structure.

questions: how to avoid ibgp full mesh
how do confederations avoid ibgp full mesh
subtitle: How BGP confederations divide a large autonomous system while hiding the divisions externally.

tldr.problem: BGP's full-mesh requirement means every speaker in one autonomous system needs a session with every other speaker, which becomes difficult to maintain at scale.
tldr.mechanism: A confederation divides the system into Member-ASes. Internal peers use Member-AS numbers and new AS_PATH segment types, while outside peers see the confederation identifier.
tldr.outcome: Confederations reduce internal BGP connection requirements and can help with policy control. RFC 5065 obsoletes RFC 3065 and is updated by RFC 9774.

today: RFC 5065 is a Draft Standard published in August 2007. It obsoletes RFC 3065 and is updated by RFC 9774.

sections.title: The Full-Mesh Scaling Problem
sections.content:
The Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) requires every BGP speaker inside one autonomous system (AS) to maintain an Internal BGP (IBGP) session with every other speaker. With n speakers, that requires n*(n-1)/2 unique sessions. The RFC describes this as a scaling problem for large networks.

BGP confederations divide one large AS into smaller systems and present the collection as one AS to external peers. The RFC also notes that subdivision may help routing-policy control, but can make AS_PATH policy and external peering more complex.
sections.plainLanguage: As the number of BGP speakers grows, the full mesh requires many internal sessions. A confederation divides the speakers into smaller systems and reduces the connections needed between them.

sections.title: Confederations and Member Systems
sections.content:
An AS Confederation is a collection of autonomous systems advertised as one AS number to peers outside the confederation. That externally visible number is the AS Confederation Identifier. Inside the confederation, each Member-AS has its own Member-AS Number.

Member-AS numbers are visible only within the confederation. External peers see the confederation identifier instead of the internal subdivision. This hides internal topology, but the RFC warns that subdivision can complicate routing policy and may affect optimal routing.
sections.plainLanguage: Inside the confederation, each Member-AS has its own number. Outside it, BGP peers see the shared confederation identifier.

sections.title: The Confederation AS_PATH Segments
sections.content:
The BGP AS_PATH attribute contains path segments. Each segment has a type, a length, and a list of autonomous systems. Base BGP defines AS_SET, an unordered set, and AS_SEQUENCE, an ordered sequence.

RFC 5065 adds AS_CONFED_SEQUENCE, an ordered list of Member-ASes traversed inside the confederation, and AS_CONFED_SET, the unordered equivalent. The RFC assigns them segment type values 3 and 4, respectively.
sections.plainLanguage: The AS_PATH records which autonomous systems a route has crossed. Two new segment types record Member-ASes that the route crossed inside the confederation.

sections.title: Route Advertisement and Path Selection
sections.content:
A confederation member uses its Member-AS Number with peers inside the confederation and its Confederation Identifier with outside peers. When sending a route to another Member-AS, it adds its Member-AS number to a leading AS_CONFED_SEQUENCE or creates such a segment. When sending outside, it removes all confederation segments and adds the Confederation Identifier to an AS_SEQUENCE.

A speaker treats its own Confederation Identifier in the path, or its own Member-AS Number in a confederation segment, as a route loop. During path selection, confederation segments should not count toward AS_PATH length. Routes learned from peers anywhere inside the same confederation are treated as internal.
sections.plainLanguage: Internal advertisements record Member-AS numbers, while outside advertisements remove those details and use the confederation identifier. BGP also checks the path for its own number to detect a loop.

sections.title: Rejecting Invalid Confederation Paths
sections.content:
A speaker must not send AS_CONFED_SET or AS_CONFED_SEQUENCE segments to a peer outside the confederation. If a speaker receives those segments from an outside neighbor, it treats the UPDATE as having a malformed AS_PATH.

A confederation peer in a different Member-AS must send an UPDATE whose first path segment is AS_CONFED_SEQUENCE. If that condition is not met, the receiving speaker also treats the path as malformed. These error rules apply to all BGP speakers, not only confederation members.
sections.plainLanguage: Confederation-only path details must stay inside the confederation. A speaker treats those details arriving from outside, or an invalid internal path, as an error.

sections.title: Compatibility and Deployment Risks
sections.content:
Every speaker inside a confederation must recognize the two new AS_PATH segment types. A speaker that does not support them generates a BGP notification for a malformed AS_PATH. Speakers outside the confederation do not need to support the extensions because the new segments are removed before routes leave.

The RFC reports that confederations had been deployed and supported by multiple vendors. Incorrect configuration can duplicate routing information, waste resources, cause route flaps, and delay convergence. Confederations can also contribute to persistent route oscillation; operators must take care with Multi-Exit Discriminator (MED) values and tie-breaking policies.
sections.plainLanguage: All BGP speakers inside the confederation need support for the new path segments. Incorrect configuration can cause duplicate routes, repeated route changes, or slow convergence.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC states that confederations do not change the security issues already present in BGP. It adds no security protection of its own.

Security considerations for the underlying BGP protocol remain applicable to deployments that use confederations.
sections.plainLanguage: Confederations do not change BGP's underlying security issues and do not add protection against them.
